terms.def: The oneness of God in worship, lordship and His names and attributes; the root of the religion and the centre of every message.
Faith in God, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and divine decree — good and bad from it.
Submitting to God by following His guidance; it covers belief, speech and action.
To worship God as if you see Him — for even if you do not see Him, He sees you.
The testification that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His messenger; the entry into the faith.
Prayer fixed at five times a day; the pillar of the faith and the first thing a servant is judged on.
An obligatory share of wealth given to the poor; it purifies money and makes it grow.
Fasting from dawn to sunset during Ramadan in obedience to God.
The pilgrimage to the House of God in its prescribed seasons, for those able to make the journey.
What is attributed to the Prophet ﷺ in sayings, actions and approvals; the second source of law.
Putting everything in its rightful place; binding on rulers and ruled alike, and the rule of judgement.
Mercy and tenderness toward those in need; an attribute of God and a quality of the believers.
Perfecting one’s duty to God and to people — including kinship and honouring parents.
Refraining from revenge when one has the power to take it; a sign of strength, not weakness.
Words matching reality; a path to Paradise and a sign of sincere intention.
Safeguarding what one is trusted with — wealth, secrets or office; a condition for stewardship on earth.
A binding pledge linking its owner to a duty, contract or covenant.
Intercession on the Day of Judgement by God’s permission — by prophets, scholars and believers.
The Day of Resurrection, judgement, Paradise and Hell; the goal of belief and the root of hope.
One who governs God’s earth by His command; a description of humanity’s stewardship of it.
Calling people to what religion agrees is good; a communal duty and a rule for a healthy society.
Turning people away from what religion agrees is evil; a condition for good to endure.
Analogical reasoning: extending a ruling to a new case sharing its cause; a source of law.
Exerting scholarly effort to derive a ruling from its evidence; required when no explicit text exists.
